page: Amazon Web Services c7gd.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 design running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, translating to 2.0 GB per core, and is managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7gd.12xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Geekbench multi-core scores both rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with cached small-block read speeds reaching 4652.94 GB/sec and large-block uncached write speeds at 116.34 GB/sec, earning a top-tier PassMark memory score. Database and key-value store performance are also robust, as evidenced by a strong PassMark database operations score and Redis SET operations reaching 76.38 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and certain text processing tasks fall into the average tier, and text generation for very small LLM models is relatively weak.

The instance offers high resource density and cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from ARM64 architecture and local NVMe storage. By utilizing dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers predictable execution. The combination of high memory bandwidth, fast local storage, and strong multi-core performance makes the c7gd.12xlarge highly suitable for high-performance web serving, database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and medium-scale language model inference.

The lack of simultaneous multithreading ensures predictable execution for demanding workloads. The c7gd.12xlarge is highly efficient for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, database operations, and medium-scale machine learning inference where local high-speed storage and high memory throughput are required.
